note:
David Shaw Ramsay and his sister Wilhelmina, both single and living on their own means, with three servants at **16 Pelham Terrace** on the 1891 return - the house now numbered **23 Newcastle Drive** (#219). Transcribed from the census image by Claude at A. Hagues's request. 23 Newcastle Drive held only 1921, so 1891 is free, and none of the five was in the record.

**The placement is by the conversion rule**, 39 minus the Pelham Terrace number, fixed by two confirmed pairs - 12 to 27 (Glendower, the Fosters) and 24 to 15. 39 - 16 = 23. See [[newcastle-drive-pelham-terrace-numbers]].

Both Ramsays were born at Edinburgh. They are linked as brother and sister, which the return states outright.

**Readings to check:** Wilhelmina's age, which I read as 76 against her brother's 66 - an elder sister by ten years is perfectly possible but the figure is worth a second look; and her middle initials, read as M A. John James Toaler, the fourteen-year-old page, is returned as born at South Shields with Northumberland given as the county, though South Shields is in Durham; both are recorded as written. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 16 Pelham Terrace (now 23 Newcastle Drive), read from the census image supplied by A. Hagues.
